mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate reduces the discount rate applied to equity cash flows, increasing the present value of future earnings and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly year-over-year CPIAUCSL increase exceeding 3.5% signals persistent inflation, prompting delayed rate cuts and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 3.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate and rise in nonfarm payrolls signals labor market tightening that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE declines and PAYEMS rises, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a high labor market tightness regime (UNRATE < 3.5% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% MoM), the Federal Reserve delays rate cuts, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE < 3.5% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% MoM, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher monthly housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer demand for housing, which correlates with increased consumer spending and corporate revenue, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST is above its 12-month moving average, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.0 signals a weakening manufacturing sector, reducing corporate profits and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 100.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS signals aggressive monetary tightening, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL rises and FEDFUNDS rises, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), the Federal Reserve's rate hikes compress equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
